lead.t: Acanthosis nigricans (dark pigmentation of skin creases in the nape of the neck especially), a sign of insulin resistance, is present in the majority of patients with T2DM and is accompanied by a relative hyperinsulinemia at the time of the diagnosis.

snip.t: Acanthosis nigricans (dark pigmentation of skin creases in the nape of the neck especially), a sign of insulin resistance, is present in the majority of patients with T2DM and is accompanied by a relative hyperinsulinemia at the time of the diagnosis.

Metformin, an oral antihyperglycemic commonly used to treat T2DM is sometimes used clinically as an adjunct therapy in T1DM patients with evidence of significant insulin resistance (i.e., obesity, insulin requirements >1.2 units/kg/day, acanthosis nigricans on exam).
Acanthosis nigricans (hyperpigmented velvety plaques on neck, axillae): Marker of chronic hyperinsulinaemia and insulin resistance.
Skin inspection: Acanthosis nigricans, striae, xanthelasma, skin tags — Hyperinsulinaemia stimulates keratinocyte proliferation (acanthosis) and lipid deposition (xanthelasma).
Paraneoplastic signs: acanthosis nigricans, Trousseau's sign (migratory thrombophlebitis, also in pancreatic cancer), dermatomyositis.

snip.t: Complications: type 2 diabetes and insulin resistance (acanthosis nigricans), hypertension, dyslipidaemia, fatty liver disease, obstructive sleep apnoea, slipped upper femoral epiphysis and knee pain, early puberty, and psychological problems.
